title: Review feedback without a branch full of 'address comments' commits
summary: Three rounds of review feedback, each fixing a different earlier commit. Use --fixup and --autosquash so the branch stays exactly as reviewable as it was on day one.
mental_model: `git commit --fixup=<sha>` writes a commit whose subject is literally `fixup! <that commit's subject>`. `rebase --autosquash` reads those subjects, reorders each fixup to sit under its target, and marks it fixup in the todo list. The convention is the whole mechanism.

steps.title: The branch as the reviewer sees it
steps.why: Three clean commits, one concern each. This is the state you want to still be in after review — not three commits plus five commits of corrections.

steps.title: Feedback: the dosing calculation needs validation
steps.why: `--fixup=<sha>` marks this commit as belonging to an earlier one. It commits normally, so nothing is lost if you stop here — but the subject line carries the instruction for later.
steps.expect: A commit literally titled 'fixup! Add dosing calculation'.

verify.label: the fixup commit is labelled against its target
verify.hint: git commit --fixup=<sha of the dosing commit>

steps.title: Feedback: the pump driver needs a guard too
steps.why: A second fixup, aimed at a different earlier commit. They can arrive in any order and target any commit on the branch — autosquash sorts it out later.
steps.expect: Five commits: three real, two fixups pointing backwards.

steps.title: Feedback: the schedule commit needs a better message
steps.why: `--squash` is the sibling of `--fixup`: it folds in the same way but keeps both messages for you to edit. Use it when the original message was wrong, not just the code.

actions.run: sh -c 'git commit -q --squash=$(git log --format=%H --grep="Add dosing schedule" -1) -m "also pin the timezone"'

steps.expect: Six commits, three of them marked fixup! or squash!.

steps.title: Preview what autosquash will do
steps.why: The todo list is what rebase would open in your editor. Each fixup has been moved directly beneath its target and marked. Reading this before running is how you build trust in the command.
steps.expect: The raw order — fixups at the end, before autosquash rearranges them.

steps.title: Run the autosquash
steps.why: `--autosquash` reorders and folds everything in one pass. Here the todo editor is scripted to accept the arrangement unchanged, which is exactly what you would do by saving and quitting.
steps.expect: Back to three commits, each containing its own fix.

verify.label: the branch is back to three commits

steps.title: Make it the default
steps.why: `rebase.autoSquash true` means plain `git rebase -i main` always honours fixups. `rebase.autoStash true` stashes and restores uncommitted work around a rebase. Both remove a step you would otherwise forget.

verify.label: autosquash is on by default now
the branch is three reviewable commits again
verify.hint: git commit --fixup=<sha> for each round, then git rebase -i --autosquash main

verify.label: the dosing fix landed inside the dosing commit
the pump fix landed inside the pump commit
autosquash is configured as the default

pitfalls: `--fixup` needs the target commit's sha. `git log --oneline` then copy, or use `--fixup=:/some words` to match by message.
Autosquash only works when the target commit is inside the rebase range. Fixing up a commit already on main does nothing.
Push the fixup commits during review so the reviewer can see the individual responses, then autosquash just before merge. Squashing early hides what you changed.
`fixup!` matching is by subject line. Reword the target commit and its fixups stop finding it.
cheatsheet: a commit that will fold into an earlier one
target by message instead of sha
fold in, but keep both messages
stash and restore around a rebase
